Crippling Strike.description: A rogue who possesses this ability strikes with such accuracy during sneak attacks that her blows debilitate the target. Any opponent who takes damage from one of her sneak attacks also suffers 2 points of Strength damage. Ability score points lost this way recover naturally at a rate of 1 point per day per affected ability.

Defensive Roll.description: The rogue learns to absorb the impact of a potentially fatal strike. Once per day, when a weapon or physical blow (not a spell or special ability) in combat would reduce her to 0 or fewer hit points, she may attempt to roll with the impact. She makes a Reflex saving throw with a DC equal to the damage dealt. On a success, she suffers only half the damage; on a failure, she takes the full amount. She must be aware of the incoming attack and able to respond - if her Dexterity bonus to AC is denied, she cannot use this ability. Because this situation would not ordinarily permit a Reflex save for half damage, her evasion ability has no effect on the defensive roll.

Evasion.description: Beginning at 2nd level, a rogue gains the agility to completely avoid certain magical and extraordinary attacks. When she succeeds on a Reflex saving throw against an effect that would normally deal half damage on a successful save (such as a dragon's breath or an explosion spell), she takes no damage whatsoever. This ability only functions while the rogue wears light armor or no armor at all. A rogue who is helpless (for example, unconscious or paralyzed) cannot benefit from this ability.

Feat.description: A rogue may choose to gain a bonus feat instead of selecting a special ability.

Improved Evasion.description: This functions identically to evasion, with the additional benefit that on a failed Reflex saving throw against effects like dragon breath or explosion spells, the rogue takes only half damage rather than full damage. A helpless rogue (such as one who is unconscious or paralyzed) gains no benefit from improved evasion.

Improved Uncanny Dodge.description: At 8th level or higher, a rogue can no longer be flanked. She responds to enemies positioned on opposite sides of her just as readily as to a single opponent. This means other rogues cannot use flanking to sneak attack her, unless the attacking rogue has at least four more rogue levels than she does. If the character previously gained uncanny dodge through a different class, she automatically receives improved uncanny dodge instead, and levels from all classes that provide uncanny dodge are combined when determining the minimum rogue level needed to flank her.

Opportunist.description: Once each round, the rogue may take an attack of opportunity against a foe who has just been hit for damage in melee by another character. This uses up the rogue's attack of opportunity for the round. Even if the rogue has the Combat Reflexes feat, she can only use this ability once per round.

Skill Mastery.description: The rogue attains such proficiency with certain skills that she can perform them reliably under any circumstances. When she gains this ability, she chooses a number of skills equal to 3 + her Intelligence modifier. For those chosen skills, she may take 10 on skill checks even when stress or distractions would normally make that impossible. This special ability can be selected multiple times, with new skills chosen each time.

Slippery Mind.description: The rogue develops a mental resilience that helps her escape magical compulsions. If she is subjected to an enchantment spell or effect and fails her saving throw, she may attempt the save again 1 round later at the same DC. She receives only this single additional attempt.

Sneak Attack.description: When a rogue catches a foe who cannot effectively defend against her strike, she can target a vulnerable point to inflict additional damage. Specifically, the rogue deals extra damage whenever her target would be denied its Dexterity bonus to AC (regardless of whether the target actually possesses such a bonus) or whenever she is flanking the target. This bonus damage starts at 1d6 at 1st level and increases by an additional 1d6 for every two rogue levels gained after that. If a sneak attack results in a critical hit, the extra damage dice are not multiplied. For ranged attacks to qualify as sneak attacks, the target must be within 30 feet; beyond that distance, the rogue cannot aim with sufficient precision. Using a sap (blackjack) or an unarmed strike, a rogue may choose to deal nonlethal damage with a sneak attack instead of lethal damage. She cannot, however, use a lethal weapon to deal nonlethal sneak attack damage, even by accepting the normal -4 penalty, since executing a sneak attack requires her to use her weapon to its fullest capability. Sneak attacks are only effective against living creatures that have identifiable anatomies - undead, constructs, oozes, plants, and incorporeal creatures have no vital areas to target. Creatures immune to critical hits are likewise immune to sneak attacks. The rogue needs clear enough sight of the target to identify a weak point and must be able to physically reach it. She cannot perform a sneak attack against a creature that has concealment or against body parts of a creature whose vital organs are out of reach.

Trap Sense.description: Starting at 3rd level, a rogue develops a heightened awareness of danger posed by traps. She receives a +1 bonus on Reflex saves to avoid traps and a +1 dodge bonus to AC against trap attacks. These bonuses increase to +2 at 6th level, +3 at 9th level, +4 at 12th level, +5 at 15th level, and +6 at 18th level. Trap sense bonuses from different classes stack with one another.

Trapfinding.description: Only rogues are able to use the Search skill to detect traps with a Difficulty Class above 20. Locating a nonmagical trap requires a DC of at least 20, potentially higher for particularly well-concealed ones. Detecting a magical trap has a DC equal to 25 + the spell level used in its creation. Likewise, only rogues can employ the Disable Device skill to disarm magical traps. A magical trap typically has a Disable Device DC of 25 + the spell level that created it. If a rogue exceeds a trap's DC by 10 or more on her Disable Device check, she can analyze the trap's mechanism and lead her companions past it safely without actually disarming it.

Uncanny Dodge.description: From 4th level onward, a rogue can instinctively react to threats before she would normally perceive them. She keeps her Dexterity bonus to AC (if she has one) even when caught flat-footed or attacked by an unseen assailant. She does, however, lose this bonus if she is rendered immobile. If the rogue has already gained uncanny dodge from another class (such as having at least two barbarian levels), she instead automatically receives improved uncanny dodge.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: Rogues have proficiency with all simple weapons, as well as the hand crossbow, rapier, sap, shortbow, and short sword. They are proficient with light armor but not with any type of shield.

overrides.description: No two rogues are exactly alike. Some operate as stealthy burglars, while others rely on charm and deception. Still others serve as scouts, spies, diplomats, or enforcers. What unites them is their exceptional versatility, quick thinking, and natural resourcefulness. Generally speaking, rogues excel at obtaining things others would rather keep hidden: access to secured vaults, safe navigation through lethal traps, confidential military plans, a sentry's confidence, or the coins in a stranger's pouch. Rogues take up adventuring for the same reasons they pursue most endeavors: personal gain. Some seek treasure; others desire the growth that comes from experience. A few chase renown, while others prefer notoriety. Many simply relish a good challenge. Working out how to circumvent a trap or bypass a warning system is deeply satisfying for a number of rogues. They are exceptionally skilled individuals who can focus their training across a wide variety of disciplines. Although they cannot match many other classes in direct combat, rogues know precisely where to strike for maximum effect, and their sneak attacks can inflict devastating damage. Rogues possess an almost supernatural instinct for sensing and avoiding danger. As they advance in skill, veteran rogues develop near-mystical abilities rooted in their mastery of stealth, evasion, and precision strikes. Furthermore, while rogues lack the ability to cast spells innately, they can convincingly improvise well enough to activate scrolls, wands, and nearly any other magical item.

Basically, the rogue's attack deals extra damage any time her target would be denied a Dexterity bonus to AC (whether the target actually has a Dexterity bonus or not), or when the rogue flanks her target. This extra damage is 1d6 at 1st level, and it increases by 1d6 every two rogue levels thereafter. Should the rogue score a critical hit with a sneak attack, this extra damage is not multiplied. Ranged attacks can count as sneak attacks only if the target is within 30 feet. A rogue can't strike with deadly accuracy from beyond that range. She cannot use a weapon that deals lethal damage to deal nonlethal damage in a sneak attack, not even with the usual -4 penalty, because she must make optimal use of her weapon in order to execute a sneak attack. A rogue can sneak attack only living creatures with discernible anatomies-undead, constructs, oozes, plants, and incorporeal creatures lack vital areas to attack.
